hypothesis: A scripted, configuration-driven dataset pipeline that jointly generates (a) clean, (b) watermarked, and (c) watermark-removal-attacked media—with explicit labels and provenance metadata—can be made reproducible across machines and time such that independent runs on the same configuration yield bitwise-identical manifests and statistically-stable dataset characteristics, while supporting realistic and adversarial coverage required for downstream watermark removal detection research.

baseline.description: Ad hoc dataset construction using one-off scripts and manual steps, without a unified pipeline, versioned configuration, or explicit provenance tracking.
characteristics: Watermarked and attacked variants created via loosely coordinated scripts, often run manually or in notebooks.
No single source of truth for dataset definition (transform choices, watermark parameters, attack recipes).
Limited or inconsistent metadata: labels may exist, but attack provenance, watermark parameters, and licensing fields are incomplete or missing.
Non-reproducible sampling and ordering (random seeds not fixed, no manifest files), making it difficult to re-generate the exact dataset for audits or follow-up experiments.
No enforced separation between synthetic and real content, and no explicit dataset versioning or governance metadata.

treatment.description: A unified, configuration-driven dataset generation and governance pipeline implemented in the companion repository under `datasets/ch4_watermark_pipeline/`.
key_properties: Single CLI entry point that reads a versioned YAML configuration specifying data sources, watermarking schemes, attack recipes, splits, and output formats.
Deterministic sampling and processing controlled by explicit random seeds; generation produces a manifest (`manifest.jsonl`) with cryptographic hashes for all files.

Rich metadata per asset: watermark presence, attack type and parameters, content source and license, synthetic vs. real, generation pipeline version, and lineage identifiers linking variants to a common base.
Support for both clean, watermarked, and attacked variants per base item, enabling paired comparisons in downstream detection experiments.
Built-in sanity checks and summary statistics (e.g., class balance, attack distribution, modality distribution) that can be re-computed to validate dataset integrity over time.
Dataset versioning via a semantic version tag and a governance metadata file (`DATASET_CARD.md` or `dataset_card.json`) capturing scope, limitations, and known biases.

workloads.name: workload_synthetic_images_only
workloads.description: Generate a fully synthetic image dataset where both content and watermarks are created by the pipeline, then simulate multiple removal attacks.

inputs.base_media_source: Synthetic images rendered or procedurally generated by scripts under `data_sources/synthetic_images/` or by a configured generative model (e.g., Stable Diffusion) with a fixed prompt list.

artifacts: Directory tree under `artifacts/ch4_synthetic_images_only/vX.Y/` containing `clean/`, `watermarked/`, and `attacked/` subdirectories.
`manifest.jsonl` capturing one record per asset with full metadata and hashes.
Governance materials: `DATASET_CARD.md` describing this dataset variant.

workloads.name: workload_mixed_real_and_synthetic
workloads.description: Generate a mixed dataset combining properly licensed real images with synthetic ones, enabling analysis of distribution shift and realism effects.

inputs.base_media_source: Combination of curated, licensed real images in `data_sources/real_images/` and synthetic images generated as in `workload_synthetic_images_only`.

artifacts: Directory `artifacts/ch4_mixed_real_synthetic/vX.Y/` with modality and source-based partitions (`real/`, `synthetic/`).
Extended `manifest.jsonl` indicating `source_type` (real/synthetic) and licensing info for each item.
`source_balance_report.json` summarizing contributions by source and content category.
Updated `DATASET_CARD.md` explicitly describing synthetic vs. real composition and licensing assumptions.

workloads.name: workload_video_segments
workloads.description: Generate a smaller but representative video dataset composed of short clips with watermarks and removal attacks applied frame-wise and temporally, to prepare for Chapter 7.

inputs.base_media_source: Short video clips (e.g., 3–10 seconds) stored under `data_sources/videos/`, either synthetic or real with confirmed licensing.

artifacts: Directory `artifacts/ch4_video_segments/vX.Y/` containing raw, watermarked, and attacked clips organized by `split/clip_id/variant/`.
Video-oriented `manifest.jsonl` with clip-level and frame-level metadata, including frame counts and temporal attack parameters.
A `stats_temporal_consistency.json` file summarizing how watermark/removal patterns vary across frames.

workloads.name: workload_governance_and_bias_audit
workloads.description: Run the pipeline on previously generated datasets to produce governance and bias-oriented reports without regenerating media (read-only over manifests).

artifacts: An updated global `datasets_index.json` listing all dataset variants, versions, and high-level stats for downstream discovery.
Sanity-check logs confirming manifest integrity (hash re-checks) and parameter coverage.

data_controls: Base media sets (`data_sources/*`) are read-only during experiments; pipeline writes only to `artifacts/` or a specified output directory.
All base media must have explicit license metadata recorded in `data_sources/metadata.jsonl` or equivalent, with automated checks rejecting items lacking required licensing fields.
Synthetic media generators must be configured with deterministic seeds and fixed prompt lists stored under version control.
process_controls: All runs must be initiated via the CLI entry point (e.g., `python -m datasets.ch4_watermark_pipeline.run` or `scripts/run_dataset_pipeline.py`), not via ad hoc Python snippets.
Each run must specify an explicit configuration file and a dataset version tag (e.g., `--config configs/ch4/synthetic_images_only.yaml --dataset_version v1.0.0`).
Random seeds used for sampling, watermarking, and attacks must be logged in a run metadata file (e.g., `run_metadata.json`).
environment_controls: Pinned Python and library versions via `environment.yml` or `requirements.txt` under `envs/ch4_environment/`.
Optional containerized environment (e.g., `docker/ch4.Dockerfile`) for full isolation and OS-level reproducibility.
Consistent hardware execution where possible; if GPU is used for model-based attacks, GPU model and driver versions must be logged.

metrics.name: num_items_total
metrics.description: Total number of generated assets (across clean, watermarked, and attacked variants).

metrics.name: num_base_items
metrics.description: Number of unique base media items (before watermarking and attacks).

metrics.name: variant_ratio_clean_watermarked_attacked
metrics.description: Proportion of clean vs. watermarked vs. attacked items in the final dataset.

metrics.name: class_balance_watermark_presence
metrics.description: Balance across labels indicating watermark presence/absence (e.g., clean, watermarked, removed, uncertain).

metrics.name: attack_coverage_by_type
metrics.description: Distribution of attacked items across different attack types (e.g., compression, geometric, inpainting, diffusion-based).

metrics.name: source_type_distribution
metrics.description: Distribution of items by source type (e.g., real vs. synthetic; content domain if available).

metrics.name: seed_reproducibility_consistency
metrics.description: Degree to which repeated runs with the same configuration and seed regenerate identical manifests (e.g., via hash comparisons).

metrics.name: metadata_completeness_rate
metrics.description: Fraction of items whose metadata records contain all required fields defined in the evidence schema.

metrics.name: file_integrity_rate
metrics.description: Fraction of files whose stored hash matches recomputed hash when validating an existing dataset.

metrics.name: pipeline_runtime
metrics.description: Total wall-clock time to generate the dataset for a given workload.

metrics.name: storage_footprint
metrics.description: Total size of the generated dataset on disk.

metrics.name: governance_doc_coverage
metrics.description: Whether required governance documentation artifacts (e.g., dataset card, license summary, bias report) are present and pass basic validation.

reproducibility: For each workload, two independent runs with the same configuration file, dataset version, and random seed produce `manifest.jsonl` files that match exactly (byte-for-byte) or produce records whose sorted content (excluding transient fields like timestamps) is identical. Target: `seed_reproducibility_consistency >= 0.999`.

For workloads where external model-based generators introduce non-determinism (e.g., non-deterministic GPU ops), any residual variability must be documented, and a stable subset with deterministic behavior must still satisfy the strict reproducibility criterion.
coverage_and_balance: For `workload_synthetic_images_only` and `workload_mixed_real_and_synthetic`, the ratio of clean:watermarked:attacked items is within ±5 percentage points of the configured target ratios (e.g., 1:1:2 by default).
`class_balance_watermark_presence` for major label categories (e.g., watermarked vs. non-watermarked) is not more imbalanced than 70:30 unless explicitly configured otherwise.

For each configured attack type, at least a minimum number of items (e.g., 200 per attack type for 1000 base images in synthetic workload) is successfully generated, ensuring coverage for downstream model training.
metadata_and_integrity: `metadata_completeness_rate >= 0.99` for required fields defined in the evidence schema.
`file_integrity_rate = 1.0` immediately after dataset creation (no mismatch between stored and computed hashes).
Governance artifacts (`DATASET_CARD.md`, license summary, basic bias report) exist and pass schema or content checks, i.e., `governance_doc_coverage = 1`.
practicality: For the default scale parameters in the provided configs, end-to-end pipeline runtime on a reference machine (specified in `required_environment`) is less than 2 hours for image workloads and less than 4 hours for the video workload.
Storage footprint for synthetic workloads remains within documented bounds for the chosen base counts (e.g., under 50 GB for specified defaults).

failure_modes.name: non_reproducible_outputs
failure_modes.description: Repeated runs with the same configuration and seed produce different manifests or different file hashes.
potential_causes: Use of non-deterministic library routines (e.g., some GPU kernels) without deterministic mode enabled.
Unseeded random operations inside watermarking or attack functions.
Use of system time or unordered directory listing to drive sampling.
failure_modes.detection: Compare `manifest.jsonl` and file hashes from two runs; compute `seed_reproducibility_consistency`.
mitigations: Enable deterministic flags for PyTorch / TensorFlow when used in attack generation.
Ensure all random number generation passes through a single seeded RNG interface in the pipeline.
Sort input file lists and make pipeline traversal order deterministic.

failure_modes.name: metadata_incompleteness
failure_modes.description: Significant fraction of items missing key metadata fields (e.g., label, attack parameters, license info).
potential_causes: Code paths in attack or watermark modules failing to return structured parameter descriptions.
Base media missing or having malformed licensing metadata.
Backward-incompatible changes to evidence schema without corresponding code updates.
failure_modes.detection: Compute `metadata_completeness_rate` and surface any missing fields in validation logs.
mitigations: Add strict validation steps that fail the run when required fields are missing for more than a small threshold (e.g., 0.1%).
Introduce default/fallback metadata only when semantically valid and log all uses of fallbacks.
Version the evidence schema and provide migration scripts for old manifests.

failure_modes.name: insufficient_attack_coverage
failure_modes.description: Some configured attack types produce few or no examples, leading to skewed or incomplete attack distributions.
potential_causes: Runtime errors or timeouts in specific attack modules.
Misconfiguration (e.g., overly strict filtering of attacked outputs).
Dependence on external services or models that are unavailable.
failure_modes.detection: Analyze `attack_coverage_by_type` metric per manifest; flag attack types with counts below minimum thresholds.
mitigations: Implement graceful fallback logic (e.g., skip problematic attack types with explicit logging) and optional re-run attempts.
Include unit and integration tests for each attack recipe under test workloads.
Allow configuration of per-attack timeouts and local model fallbacks.

failure_modes.name: governance_artifact_missing_or_invalid
failure_modes.description: Dataset card, license summaries, or bias reports are not generated or fail validation checks.
potential_causes: Governance generation step not wired into the main pipeline or erroneously skipped for certain configs.
Schema or template changes not reflected in report generation code.
failure_modes.detection: Governance validation script checks for presence and basic structure of required artifacts; `governance_doc_coverage` becomes 0.
mitigations: Make governance generation a mandatory pipeline stage, failing runs if artifacts cannot be produced.
Track governance artifact schemas under version control and include tests that regenerate them on sample manifests.

failure_modes.name: licensing_or_source_mislabeling
failure_modes.description: Real or synthetic sources are mislabeled or licensing metadata is incomplete, undermining compliance.
potential_causes: Incorrect or missing entries in source metadata files.
Re-use of sample configs on new data sources without updating licensing fields.
failure_modes.detection: Validation step checks required license fields for all real sources and that `source_type` is consistent with source directories.
mitigations: Enforce strict checks that any real image or video must have explicit, validated licensing metadata or else be excluded.
Require manual review and approval of new source directories, recorded in governance logs.

hardware.cpu: 4+ physical cores (x86_64 or ARM64) with AVX or equivalent recommended.

gpu_optional.recommended: 1 x NVIDIA GPU with 8+ GB VRAM for model-based attacks and synthetic generation.
gpu_optional.note: If no GPU is available, configs should be adjusted to disable or downscale model-based attacks.

software.os: Linux (Ubuntu 20.04+ recommended) or macOS 13+; Windows supported via WSL2 or native if compatible with dependencies.
software.python: Python 3.10 or 3.11, installed via conda or pyenv.
software.dependencies: Install from `envs/ch4_environment/requirements.txt` or `environment.yml` in the repository.
core_libraries: pydantic or marshmallow for schema validation
Optionally: torch or tensorflow, diffusers, transformers for model-based synthetic generation and attacks

run_instructions:
1. Clone the repository:
   git clone https://github.com/bookauthority/ai-watermark-removal-detection.git
   cd ai-watermark-removal-detection

2. Set up the Python environment (example with conda):
   conda env create -f envs/ch4_environment/environment.yml
   conda activate awrd-ch4

3. (Optional) Pull or prepare base media sources:
   - Place licensed real images under `data_sources/real_images/` with metadata in `data_sources/real_images/metadata.jsonl`.
   - Place or generate synthetic prompts and assets under `data_sources/synthetic_images/` as specified in `configs/ch4/*.yaml`.
   - Place licensed video clips under `data_sources/videos/` with metadata in `data_sources/videos/metadata.jsonl`.

4. Run the synthetic image-only workload:
   python -m datasets.ch4_watermark_pipeline.run \
       --config configs/ch4/synthetic_images_only.yaml \
       --dataset_version v1.0.0 \
       --output_dir artifacts/ch4_synthetic_images_only/v1.0.0 \
       --seed 12345

5. Run the mixed real+synthetic workload:
   python -m datasets.ch4_watermark_pipeline.run \
       --config configs/ch4/mixed_real_synthetic.yaml \
       --dataset_version v1.0.0 \
       --output_dir artifacts/ch4_mixed_real_synthetic/v1.0.0 \
       --seed 12345

6. Run the video segments workload (if video sources and optional GPU are available):
   python -m datasets.ch4_watermark_pipeline.run \
       --config configs/ch4/video_segments.yaml \
       --dataset_version v1.0.0 \
       --output_dir artifacts/ch4_video_segments/v1.0.0 \
       --seed 12345

7. Validate reproducibility by re-running at least one workload with the same config and seed:
   python -m datasets.ch4_watermark_pipeline.run \
       --config configs/ch4/synthetic_images_only.yaml \
       --dataset_version v1.0.0 \
       --output_dir artifacts/ch4_synthetic_images_only/v1.0.0_rerun \
       --seed 12345
   Then execute the validation script:
   python -m datasets.ch4_watermark_pipeline.validate \
       --manifest_a artifacts/ch4_synthetic_images_only/v1.0.0/manifest.jsonl \
       --manifest_b artifacts/ch4_synthetic_images_only/v1.0.0_rerun/manifest.jsonl \
       --output_report artifacts/ch4_synthetic_images_only/v1.0.0/reproducibility_report.json

8. Run governance and bias audit on existing manifests:
   python -m datasets.ch4_watermark_pipeline.governance_audit \
       --config configs/ch4/governance_audit.yaml \
       --manifests \
           artifacts/ch4_synthetic_images_only/v1.0.0/manifest.jsonl \
           artifacts/ch4_mixed_real_synthetic/v1.0.0/manifest.jsonl \
       --output_dir artifacts/ch4_governance_audit/

9. (Optional) Run tests to ensure pipeline integrity:
   pytest tests/datasets/ch4_watermark_pipeline/ -q

10. Inspect summary statistics and documentation:
   - Open `stats_summary.json` and `stats_summary.md` under each workload directory.
   - Review `DATASET_CARD.md` and governance reports to understand dataset scope, limitations, and usage notes.

manifest_record.id: string; globally unique identifier for this asset (e.g., UUID).
manifest_record.base_id: string; identifier linking all variants (clean, watermarked, attacked) derived from the same base media.
manifest_record.split: string; one of ['train', 'val', 'test'] or custom splits as configured.
manifest_record.file_path: string; relative path from repository root to the asset file.
manifest_record.file_hash: string; cryptographic hash of the file contents (e.g., SHA256 hex digest).
manifest_record.source_dataset: string; optional tag indicating the original collection (e.g., 'internal_stock_v1').

license.notes: string; free-text notes about licensing constraints, if any.

labels.attack_type: string or null; one of configured attack identifiers (e.g., 'jpeg_80', 'crop_10pct', 'diffusion_resynthesis') for attacked variants.
labels.watermark_scheme: string or null; identifier of the watermark scheme applied (e.g., 'visible_logo_bottom_right').

parameters.watermark_params: object; scheme-specific parameters such as opacity, location, frequency-domain embedding strength.
parameters.attack_params: object; attack-specific parameters such as compression quality, crop bounds, filter kernel sizes, or model prompts.
parameters.generation_params: object; for synthetic content, record generator type, model version, prompt, and RNG seed.

quality_metrics.psnr_to_base: number or null; peak signal-to-noise ratio between this variant and the clean base, where applicable.
quality_metrics.ssim_to_base: number or null; structural similarity index to the clean base, where applicable.
quality_metrics.perceptual_distance: number or null; an optional learned perceptual metric (e.g., LPIPS) if computed.

run_metadata.pipeline_version: string; semantic version of the dataset pipeline code.
run_metadata.dataset_version: string; declared dataset version tag for this run.
run_metadata.config_path: string; path to the configuration file used for this run.
run_metadata.random_seed: integer; top-level seed used for this run.
run_metadata.timestamp_utc: string; ISO 8601 timestamp when this record was generated.

environment.gpu_info: string or null; GPU model and driver version if used.

stats_summary.num_items_total: integer; total number of manifest records.
stats_summary.num_base_items: integer; total number of distinct base_ids.
stats_summary.class_balance_watermark_presence: object; keys are watermark_presence labels, values are fractions in [0,1].
stats_summary.attack_coverage_by_type: object; keys are attack_type identifiers, values are counts and/or fractions.
stats_summary.source_type_distribution: object; keys are source types (e.g., 'real', 'synthetic'), values are fractions.
stats_summary.file_integrity_rate: number; fraction of files whose stored and recomputed hashes match.
stats_summary.metadata_completeness_rate: number; fraction of manifest records with all required fields present.
stats_summary.pipeline_runtime: number; wall-clock runtime in seconds for the run.
stats_summary.storage_footprint: number; dataset size in gigabytes as measured on disk.

dataset_card.path: string; relative path to `DATASET_CARD.md` or equivalent.

bias_and_coverage_report.path: string; relative path to coverage/bias report (e.g., `coverage_report.md`).
